params.body:
## What

The worksheet page (`/fiche/{id}`) had headings in letter-spaced capitals whose names didn't say what was under them. They are now plain sentence-case headings:

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| DE DAG | Samenvatting |
| NOG ONVOLLEDIG | Ontbreekt nog |
| GEVRAAGD, EN ER WAREN ER GEEN | Hierop zei hij 'geen' |
| GEVRAAGD, KON HIJ NIET ZEGGEN | Hierop wist hij het niet |
| WAT HIJ ZELF ZEI | Zijn eigen woorden |
| RIT (departure, return, break, km for the day) | Vertrek en terug |
| UREN, MACHINES, MATERIAAL, table headers | same words, no capitals |

The items under the two "Hierop" headings are the questions, so the heading now reads as their answer.

Also:
- "Zijn eigen woorden" is left out when nothing was said. It used to read "Niets bewaard. Fiches van voor 20 augustus dragen zijn woorden nog niet."
- A 'geen' for machines, material or the site manager is no longer listed when the sheet holds one after all: a tap after the 'geen' overruled it.
- The subtitle and the signal lines use commas instead of middle dots ("vrijdag 16 oktober 2026, handarbeider, ingesproken in het Turks").

## Tests

- `OfficeAccessTest`: the page shows "Zijn eigen woorden" with his words and leaves it out without them; "Ontbreekt nog" is shown; an overruled 'geen' for machines is not listed while one for material is.
- Full suite locally: 332 of 333 passed, pint clean. The one failure is `WorksheetExportTest::test_a_week_of_worksheets_comes_out_as_a_workbook`, which fails on main on a Monday under sqlite. CI runs on MySQL.
- Checked on a local demo fiche (screenshot sent separately).
